prompt: Which of the following are the three main control problems that management control systems address?
explanation: Control problems arise because employees may not know what is expected (lack of direction), may not want to do what is expected (motivational problems), or may not be able to do it (personal limitations). Capital and competition are strategic, not control, problems.

prompt: Which of the following are ways to AVOID control problems rather than to control behaviour?
explanation: Activity elimination, automation, centralization and risk-sharing are control alternatives that avoid the problem. Setting targets is part of results controls, i.e. it controls behaviour instead of avoiding the problem.

prompt: Management control is primarily concerned with …

options.text: influencing employee behaviour so that organizational objectives are achieved

explanation: Management control is behaviour-oriented and focuses on strategy execution. Strategy formulation (strategic control) and external reporting (financial accounting) are separate concerns.

prompt: A good management control system is characterized by the fact that it …

options.text: eliminates all possible deviations from desired behaviour
makes it reasonably likely that objectives will be achieved
is forward-looking and focuses on preventing problems
has benefits that exceed its costs

explanation: Perfect control is impossible; good control means a high probability that objectives are achieved, a future orientation, and a positive cost–benefit balance.
